clue.text: Active mine boom ignoring one about a late shaft?

indicators.note: about means going round, so the rearranged letters wrap round the article a
active letters are lively, stirred into a fresh order, so the remaining letters get rearranged
ignoring something leaves it out, so a letter drops from the fodder

parts.note: one is I, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: A mining boom ignores a lonely, abandoned shaft from long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ignoring one' drops I from MINEBOOM; 'Active' rearranges the rest, MNEBOOM, into MOONBEM; 'about' puts it round A. A 'late shaft' is a shaft of light late at night, not a mineshaft.
explanation.definitionFit: A shaft of light seen at night, when the hour is late, comes from the moon.

clue.text: Copy operatic heroine (contralto)

parts.note: Mimi is the heroine of Puccini's opera La Bohème
C is a standard abbreviation for contralto in vocal scores

explanation.surface: A singer imitates an operatic heroine while singing in the contralto range.
explanation.definitionFit: To copy someone's voice or manner is to imitate them, a direct verb synonym.

clue.text: Ready to accept newspaper article's conclusion in many cases

indicators.note: accepting something takes it in, so the other letters go inside

parts.note: on means ready or going ahead, as in 'the game is on'
FT is the Financial Times

indicators.note: an article's conclusion is its final letter

explanation.surface: A newspaper is willing to run an article's conclusion in many cases.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ready' is not an adjective about the newspaper: it supplies a short word meaning 'going ahead', which 'to accept' opens to take in the paper and the article's final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that happens in many cases happens frequently, an adverbial synonym.

clue.text: I show skill surrounded by a lot of drinking

definitions.text: I show skill surrounded by a lot of drinking

indicators.note: surrounded by means placed inside, so the skill word sits within the drinking spree

parts.note: a bender is a drinking spree
art is skill, as in the art of conversation

explanation.surface: The speaker shows off a skill while surrounded by heavy drinking.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: the speaker practises their craft amid drinkers, and 'surrounded by' puts the skill inside the word for a drinking spree.
explanation.definitionFit: The person serving behind a pub counter works skilfully among people drinking a lot.

clue.text: Mounted, heading off on final trip

indicators.note: heading off means the first letter is removed

parts.note: final means last
a ride is a trip, as on horseback

explanation.surface: A rider climbs on for one final trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading off' drops the L from LAST, leaving AST.
explanation.definitionFit: Sitting with legs either side of a horse is how a mounted rider sits.

clue.text: No place in church to carry a retracted blade?

indicators.note: retracted means drawn back, so the whole assembly reads backwards

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: carrying something holds it within, so the article goes inside

parts.note: a pew is a seat in church

explanation.surface: A church bans carrying a knife with its blade drawn in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to carry' puts A in PEW to give PAEW; NO + PAEW is then 'retracted' to read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A blade such as a sword or knife is an example of an arm, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Nudge energy arc to contain luminance

parts.note: E is the symbol for energy in physics
L is the symbol for luminance
a bow is a curve or arc

explanation.surface: A physics instruction: nudge an energy arc so it holds some luminance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to contain' puts L inside BOW.
explanation.definitionFit: To nudge someone is to push them with a jab of the arm's joint, a verb sense.

clue.text: Power is retained by America? Agreeable to see removal of current power

parts.note: P is the symbol for power in physics

indicators.note: retained by means held inside, so the little word sits within the country's abbreviation

parts.note: USA is America
taken as written

indicators.note: seeing removal means a letter is taken out of the preceding word

parts.note: nice means agreeable
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: Questions whether America holds power, and whether it would agree to cutting off power supplies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Power' appears twice: the first gives the physics symbol, the last is the definition. 'retained by' and 'to see removal of' work on the pieces between.
explanation.definitionFit: This French borrowing means might or strength, and also names a show-jumping contest of strength.

clue.text: Arrange to eat roughly about 1 after information turns up

indicators.note: after means the rearranged eating words follow the information word
in a down clue, turning up means reading from bottom to top, i.e. backwards

parts.note: gen is slang for information

indicators.note: about means going round, so the rearranged letters surround the numeral
roughly signals the letters are put together loosely, in a new order

parts.note: 1 is I as a Roman numeral

explanation.surface: Instructions to sort out a meal once some news emerges.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns up' reverses GEN to NEG; 'roughly' turns TOEAT into OTATE, which goes 'about' I to give OTIATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To arrange a deal or settlement through discussion is to bargain it out, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Much of pastime will involve no associate

indicators.note: involving something takes it in, so the word no is placed inside
much of means most but not all, so the last letter goes

parts.note: a hobby is a pastime
taken as written

explanation.surface: Most of a pastime will mean having no companion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'associate' reads as a noun but is the verb, to mix socially. 'Much of' trims the pastime and 'will involve' takes the word no inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To associate or mix socially with important people is to rub shoulders, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Vehicle has men following its assessment?

indicators.note: following means the soldiers come after the test

parts.note: the MOT is the annual roadworthiness test for British vehicles
OR, other ranks, means ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: A vehicle has staff check it after its roadworthiness test.
explanation.walkthrough: The MOT is the UK's compulsory yearly safety test for cars, named after the Ministry of Transport.
explanation.definitionFit: A car is commonly called this, a near-synonym for a road vehicle.

clue.text: Transactions rising fast after initial disinvestment? That's causing concern

parts.note: TR is an abbreviation for transactions

indicators.note: disinvesting takes something away, here the first letter of the rising word

parts.note: doubling is rising fast, as prices that double

explanation.surface: A financial report frets about deals rising fast after a sell-off.
explanation.walkthrough: The financial surface hides the mechanics: 'after initial disinvestment' means the first letter of the word for rising fast has been divested.
explanation.definitionFit: Something worrying or disturbing is causing concern, an adjective synonym.

clue.text: Member of house sees anger ebbing, engrossed by revealing dance

indicators.note: engrossed by means absorbed inside, so the reversed word sits within the dance

parts.note: the cancan is a high-kicking dance that shows a lot of leg

indicators.note: ebbing means flowing back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: ire is anger

explanation.surface: A parliamentarian sees their anger subside while absorbed in a racy dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Member of house' suggests Parliament, but the house is astrological. 'ebbing' turns the anger word back and 'engrossed by' sets it inside the dance.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone born under the Crab belongs to one of the twelve astrological signs or houses.

clue.text: Society in need never existed

indicators.note: in means placed inside the need word

parts.note: want means need

explanation.surface: A society in real need was never really there at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts S inside WANT.
explanation.definitionFit: A contraction meaning 'was not', i.e. did not exist, as in 'it simply was not there'.

clue.text: Dead calm — missing ship to become insignificant

indicators.note: missing means lacking, so the ship's letters are removed

parts.note: windless weather is calm
SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: A dead calm leaves a becalmed sailor with no ship and fading hopes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing' takes SS out of WINDLESS, leaving WINDLE.
explanation.definitionFit: To shrink gradually until barely noticeable is to fade away into insignificance.

clue.text: Justifying evicting Duke to house American in very strident terms

indicators.note: housing something takes it in, so the American letter goes inside
evicting throws out, so one D leaves the word

parts.note: defending a position is justifying it

explanation.surface: Someone justifies evicting a Duke to make room for an American, in shrill language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'evicting' takes a D out of DEFENDING, giving DEFENING; 'to house' puts A inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Noise so loud it could take away one's hearing is extremely loud or shrill.

clue.text: I'm right to block nasty blog over supporting one tangled situation

indicators.note: in a down clue, supporting means sitting below, so the cricket letter comes under the numeral

parts.note: taken as written without the apostrophe

indicators.note: blocking means sitting inside and obstructing, so the right letter goes within the scrambled word
nasty signals the letters are messed up into a new order

parts.note: one is I as a Roman numeral
O is the cricket abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: A blogger steps in to block a nasty post about a sticky situation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nasty' shuffles BLOG to BOGL; 'to block' puts R inside, giving BROGL; then I with O below it ('supporting').
explanation.definitionFit: This Italian borrowing means a confused, embarrassing or complicated mess.

clue.text: Continue to request one American flowering plant

parts.note: to beg on is to keep on asking
one is I as a Roman numeral

explanation.surface: An American keeps asking for one plant in flower.
explanation.definitionFit: A popular bedding and pot plant with showy flowers, an example of a flowering plant.

clue.text: First and last of results in lovely sequence of victories

indicators.note: in means placed inside the lovely word

parts.note: glam, short for glamorous, means lovely

indicators.note: the first letter of the word results
the last letter of the word results

explanation.surface: The first and last results came in a lovely run of wins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' is not a link word here: it stays in the answer between the first and last letters of 'results', and the whole run goes 'in' the lovely word after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Winning all four major tournaments in a season, as in tennis or golf, is a full set of victories.

clue.text: Warning about billions being given to a province

indicators.note: about means going round, so the warning word encircles the billions letter

parts.note: an alert is a warning

explanation.surface: A warning goes out about billions handed over to a regional government.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts ALERT round B, giving ALBERT, then A follows.
explanation.definitionFit: This western Canadian region, capital Edmonton, is one of the country's provinces.

clue.text: A reprimand seeing book thrown is to be exciting

definitions.note: the answer is a verb meaning to make lively or fizzy, matching 'to be exciting'

indicators.note: thrown means tossed away, so the book letter is discarded

parts.note: to berate is to reprimand

explanation.surface: A telling-off in which a book gets thrown is bound to be exciting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'thrown' takes the B out of BERATE, leaving ERATE.
explanation.definitionFit: Charging something with air or gas makes it fizz, so it livens or stirs it up.

clue.text: A Democrat settling into excellent intellectual surroundings

indicators.note: settling into means going inside, so A and the party abbreviation sit within the excellent word

parts.note: ace means excellent

explanation.surface: A Democrat settles into a fine university post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'settling into' puts both the article and the party abbreviation inside the word for excellent; Dem is the usual US shortening of Democrat.
explanation.definitionFit: The academic world, the setting of universities and scholarship, surrounds intellectual life.

clue.text: Measure of deficiency: muscles subsequently not hard

parts.note: abs are abdominal muscles

indicators.note: not here means without, so the hard letter is dropped

parts.note: hence means from now on, subsequently
H is an abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A gym note: weak muscles show up later as not hard enough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' takes H from HENCE, leaving ENCE.
explanation.definitionFit: A lack or want of something is the state of it being missing, a noun synonym.

clue.text: Aliens? Our group backed sanctions

indicators.note: backed means turned back, so the pronoun reads in reverse

parts.note: we means our group
OKs are approvals or sanctions

explanation.surface: Our group supports sanctions against creatures from another world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backed' reverses WE to EW.
explanation.definitionFit: The furry forest creatures of Star Wars are non-human beings from the moon of Endor.

clue.text: Endless romance, with male passion

indicators.note: endless means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: a romance is a story

explanation.surface: An unending love affair with a man full of passion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endless' cuts STORY to STOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A violent outburst of feeling, as in a storm of rage, is a passion.

clue.text: Mostly refuse to accept paired statistical data

indicators.note: accepting takes in, so the paired word goes inside
mostly means all but the last letter

parts.note: to resist is to refuse
dual means paired or double

explanation.surface: Mostly refusing to accept paired figures from a survey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mostly' trims the last letter of the refusal word before 'to accept' takes the paired word inside it, just ahead of its final S.
explanation.definitionFit: In statistics, the differences between observed values and a fitted model's predictions are kept as data.

clue.text: Shaping of road requiring no carbon resin

indicators.note: requiring no means doing without, so the carbon letter is dropped

parts.note: camber is the slight arch shaping a road surface
C is the chemical symbol for carbon

explanation.surface: Road building that needs no carbon, just natural resin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'requiring no' takes the C from CAMBER.
explanation.definitionFit: Fossilised tree resin, golden in colour, used in jewellery.

clue.text: Husband dallies heartlessly, taking up slender young thing?

indicators.note: in a down clue, taking up means reading upwards, i.e. backwards
heartlessly means the central letter is removed

parts.note: plays means dallies or trifles

explanation.surface: A husband callously dallies and takes up with a slim young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartlessly' removes the middle A from PLAYS; 'taking up' reverses H + PLYS.
explanation.definitionFit: An air spirit, and by extension a slim graceful girl, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Telling off about religious texts of dubious origin

indicators.note: about means going round, so the rearranged letters surround the scripture abbreviation
off means wrong or out of order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: OT is the Old Testament, a set of religious texts

explanation.surface: A telling-off about religious texts whose provenance is doubtful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Telling off' looks like a scolding; 'off' rearranges TELLING to ILLGTEN, which goes 'about' OT.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods obtained dishonestly have a shady, questionable source, an adjectival synonym.

clue.text: Lines about article happen to indicate brand name

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the lines go round the other letters

parts.note: L is an abbreviation for line, so two lines are LL
a is the indefinite article
to be is to exist or happen

explanation.surface: Lines around an article happen to show a brand name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lines' gives two Ls, one for each line, and 'about' sets them either side of the article and the verb meaning happen.
explanation.definitionFit: A record company or fashion brand is known by its trade name, e.g. a designer's own.

clue.text: Good place to go, given the writer's despairing

parts.note: loo is British slang for a toilet, a place to go
the writer's means the setter's, i.e. my

explanation.surface: The writer is despairing even with a good place to go.
explanation.walkthrough: LOO is everyday British slang for a toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling dark and without hope is a pessimistic, despondent state of mind.

clue.text: Cast aspersions on revision of Chambers? I for one will intervene

indicators.note: a revision reworks these letters together into a new order, with the one dropped out

parts.note: taken as written, added to the dictionary's name
one is A, as in 'a' meaning one; it is the letter left over

explanation.surface: Someone criticises a revision of the Chambers dictionary and offers to step in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I for one will intervene': I comes into CHAMBERS in place of A (one); 'revision of' rearranges the result.
explanation.definitionFit: To tarnish someone's reputation is to smear or sully it, a verb synonym.
